The question of whether the lunar cycle affects wine taste is genuinely contested, with biodynamic practitioners and scientific researchers reaching opposing conclusions. Biodynamic winemakers and believers assert that wine tastes better on "fruit" and "flower" days and worse on "root" or "leaf" days, with some major grocery stores reportedly arranging tastings around the lunar calendar [d2]; one biodynamic source claims that "depending on the cycle of the moon, we can feel subtle changes in the sensory perception of the same wine" [d3]. However, multiple scientific studies directly contradict this view: a study by Dr. Wendy Parr involving 19 New Zealand wine professionals who blind-tasted Pinot Noir wines on fruit and root days found that "the specific day on which they were tasted did not affect how they were rated" [d7], and a 2017 PLOS ONE study similarly concluded that "the type of day had little effect on their opinions on the flavour profile of the wine" [d5]. Wine scientist Jamie Goode, cited in both [d5] and [d6], argues that "wine tastes different on different days but the differences are not that huge and the differences are more about atmospheric pressure" rather than the lunar cycle, while [d1] concludes bluntly that "lunar effects don't affect the way that wine tastes." Overall, the scientific evidence does not support the biodynamic claim, though the belief remains influential in parts of the wine industry [d4][d6].
